**Finding submitted: `missing` (critical), confidence 0.93.**

## What I found

The Agreement contains **no indemnification clause at all**. Section 20 simply does not exist:

- Paragraph flow runs contiguously from **19.5 (p0075)** directly to **"21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY" (p0076)** — the contiguous paragraph IDs confirm this is a real drafting gap, not an extraction artifact (per the planner's instruction to verify).
- Searches for `indemnify`, `defend`, and `hold harmless` return **zero operative obligations** on either party.

What survives are four **orphaned cross-references** that all presuppose an indemnity:

| Section | Dangling reference |
|---|---|
| 9.3 | termination requires "the remedies required by **Section 20.5**" |
| 19.4 | preserves remedies for "**indemnified claims**" |
| 21.3 | "its **indemnification obligations**" are Excluded Claims |
| 30.5 | preserves "vested **indemnity rights**" |

This is walk-away territory (no Vendor IP indemnity whatsoever), failing both preferred and fallback. Practically, Customer would fund its own defence of third-party infringement claims against the Services, and its recourse for Vendor-caused data incidents would be ordinary damages squeezed under the Section 21.1 cap. Section 9.3's termination right is also currently unexercisable, since the remedy standard it points to doesn't exist.

## The redline (validated `ok:true`)

Inserted a new Section 20 after 19.5 — the location the rule's own guidance prescribes and where the numbering gap sits:

- **20.1** Vendor defends/indemnifies Customer **and Affiliates**: IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct
- **20.2** Customary IP exclusions (unauthorized modification, combination, Customer specifications)
- **20.3** Customer's indemnity kept **narrow** — Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law only
- **20.4** Notice / control / cooperation, with a no-adverse-settlement carve-out
- **20.5** Procure–modify–replace–refund, deliberately numbered **20.5 so Section 9.3 resolves correctly**

## One judgment call worth flagging

I did **not** add the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap. Section 21.3 already carves indemnification obligations out of the liability cap entirely as Excluded Claims — an unlimited indemnity is strictly better for us than a 3× ceiling, so importing the fallback cap would have bargained away existing ground. Adding it would also have collided with the liability-cap rule on the same commercial term.
